For νυκτίφαντ' [appearing by night] in the copies is written νυκτίφοιτ᾽ [roaming by night], which seems correct. Furthermore, it is not likely that Aeschylus wrote ὀνείρατα [dreams] when ὀνείρασι [dreams] has just preceded. Therefore, rightly, as I think, Nauck (in Bulletin de l'Académie de Pétersbourg a. 1860 p. 241) restored νυκτίφοιτα δείματα [night-roaming terrors], which is read in Lycophron v. 225, who perhaps imitated this very passage of Aeschylus.

if δεῖμα [fear] is correctly read, which Schuetz understood as the terrible threats of the citizens, Meineke on Soph. Oed. Col. p. 251 changed to λῆμα [will, spirit].
Why does this steadfast fear (thus Triclinius for δεῖγμα [proof]) hover before my heart, the guardian of my prophetic soul?
with goad-driven terror, the wretched one.

where Dobree has δεῖ μένειν [it is necessary to remain], which perhaps the scholiast read, who noted οὐ πανταχὴ τὸ δεινὸν ἀπεῖναι φρενῶν δεῖ [it is not everywhere necessary that the terrible be absent from the mind], the beginning of which scholium perhaps were the words now attached to the scholium on v. 530, ἔσθ᾽ ὅπη δέους [there is a place where of fear], which Weil connects with the previous scholium thus: ἔσθ᾽ ὅπη δέους ὄφελος καὶ οὐ πανταχή cet. [there is a place where fear is useful and not everywhere etc.]. In imitation of these words the verses of the interpolator 701-702 were composed: καὶ μὴ τὸ δεινὸν πᾶν πόλεως ἔξω βαλεῖν · τίς γὰρ δεδοικὼς μηδὲν ἔνδικος βροτῶν; [and not to cast all fear out of the city; for who of mortals, fearing nothing, is just?]
